title: Williams v. Chesapeake Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC sustained the complaint, annulled Presbytery’s approval of the PJC report, and returned the matter to the PJC, which could dismiss the case or proceed with process under BCO 32. Other considerations raised by Williams were rendered moot.
first_summary: An indicted teaching elder challenged Chesapeake Presbytery’s approval of a PJC judgment and indefinite suspension after the PJC combined procedures under BCO 32 and BCO 38-1. The SJC sustained the complaint, annulled Presbytery’s approval, and returned the matter to the PJC because the procedural confusion prejudiced the accused’s rights. The PJC could dismiss the case or adjudicate it with process under BCO 32.
summary: An indicted teaching elder challenged Chesapeake Presbytery’s approval of a PJC judgment and indefinite suspension after the PJC blended a BCO 32 case of process with a BCO 38-1 case without process. The SJC sustained the complaint, annulled Presbytery’s approval, and returned the matter to the PJC. Because he admitted only some indicted charges, his negotiated confession could not satisfy BCO 38-1 and the conversion prejudiced his rights. The PJC may dismiss or proceed under BCO 32; the ruling does not decide whether conversion is ever permissible.

sources.supports: Case identity, issue, judgment, reasoning, remedy, qualification, and adoption of the revised decision.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: The caption and decision date appear at lines 13–15. Lines 134–136 state that the panel decision was not adopted and that the SJC approved a revised decision, 13–5.
evidence_notes.dispute: Lines 77–79 identify the challenge to Presbytery’s approval of a PJC report that conflated BCO 32 and 38-1.
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Lines 81–83 sustain the complaint, annul the approving action, and return the case to the PJC. Lines 89–130 explain that a partial plea to an indictment could not become a BCO 38-1 confession and that the confusion prejudiced the accused; other matters became moot.
evidence_notes.qualifications: Line 132 limits the reasoning to this case and declines to decide whether a case of process may ever become a case without process.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: No decision is incorporated by reference; lines 134–136 distinguish the unadopted panel decision from the approved revised decision.
